channel.title: Komposite News
channel.description: Komposite News covers artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital assets, enterprise technology and capital markets for executives, investors and builders.

item.title: The bonds say fifteen, the backlog says $104bn
item.description: CoreWeave shares fell 15.5 per cent and its 2032 bonds yielded 14.8 per cent on Wednesday, CNBC reported, as its chief executive pointed to a $104bn contract backlog.

item.title: The replicator that would need fifteen TV boxes
item.description: Anthropic researchers say small AI models may soon self-replicate across cheap IoT devices; one model did so in a simplified test that the authors call an upper bound.

item.title: Kraken's parent buys a Lithuanian bank
item.description: Payward, Kraken's parent, agreed to buy the owner of Lithuania-licensed Saldo Bank; the price is undisclosed and closing is expected in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

item.title: Half price until 30 November
item.description: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to developers at $2 and $10 per million tokens until 30 November, then $4 and $20; independent indexes rank it differently against rivals.

item.title: An option that pays on a metric, not a price
item.description: The SEC on Tuesday approved Cboe's rule change to list binary options settled on issuers' reported KPIs, treating them as securities options rather than swaps.

item.title: A wallet that passed the genuine check
item.description: Ledger says an implant in wallets sold via reseller CryptoBilis sent recovery phrases over LTE; it has paused sales across Southeast Asia and loss figures are unverified.

item.title: Forty per cent more tokens, against an unnamed GPU
item.description: Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 AI chip on Monday, saying it expects 40 per cent more tokens per megawatt than unnamed leading GPU systems; deployments start in 2027.

item.title: Binance gives miners four weeks
item.description: Binance said on Tuesday it will discontinue Binance Pool, Cloud Mining and related services on 10 November, telling miners to move hashrate to another pool.

item.title: The record penalty comes after the order
item.description: The OCC fined Bank of America $750m for deficient BSA/AML controls, its largest penalty; FinCEN's $1.2bn fine credits it, and OFAC settled for $11.7m.

item.title: A fully patched VPN, and root in three steps
item.description: Volexity says an attacker chained three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws for root access from 3 October; Ivanti fixed two under CVE-2026-104935, the third is unpatched.

item.title: Fifteen times run rate, on Modal's own numbers
item.description: AI infrastructure company Modal said it raised a $750m Series D led by Accel at a $15.75bn valuation and says its annualised run rate has passed $1bn.

item.title: Twenty million for the licence, not the app
item.description: Character.AI's parent filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware on Monday. Disney's $20m stalking-horse bid buys an IP licence; without a buyer, the platform will be wound down.

item.title: A swap on the exchange, a bet at the sportsbook
item.description: The CFTC on Friday proposed defining event contracts, including sports contracts, as swaps, and issued an interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling.

item.title: Three Yandex data centres in a week
item.description: Yandex said its Vladimir data centre was fully suspended after a drone attack on Sunday, the third on its sites in a week, with its cloud in emergency mode.

item.title: Amazon weighs a $7bn deal for Decart
item.description: Amazon is in talks to buy AI startup Decart for about $7bn, the WSJ reported on Sunday; neither company has confirmed. Bloomberg said Anthropic looked at a deal earlier.

item.title: Meta's first frontier model, priced at the frontier
item.description: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, claiming frontier parity on agent and coding tests; the API costs $4 and $20 per million tokens.

item.title: Bailey's G20 letter names bonds, private credit and AI
item.description: FSB chair Andrew Bailey's letter to the G20 flags bond volatility, private credit and AI risks and submits the board's sound practices for AI adoption.

item.title: The FSB says stablecoins are untested in a crisis
item.description: The Financial Stability Board told the G20 on Monday that global stablecoins remain untested in severe stress and urged better cross-border monitoring and data.

item.title: Eight grocery banners offline, cause unstated
item.description: Ahold Delhaize took systems offline on Monday after a network security issue; websites of eight US and Dutch banners went down and no cause or timeline was given.

item.title: The negotiator is charged with extortion
item.description: A Canadian ransomware negotiator was arrested in Pennsylvania on 8 October on extortion conspiracy charges; the complaint is sealed and the allegations are unproven.

item.title: The third NetScaler patch in eleven days
item.description: Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-107406, a 9.5-rated NetScaler SAML flaw, on Thursday; builds patched for CVE-2026-88779 remain exposed as SAML IdPs.

item.title: Three researchers fired, two accounts
item.description: OpenAI says three dismissed safety researchers broke its policies on sensitive information; the researchers' letter says the firings chill safety work.

item.title: Eight billion for 14 MHz, and the carriers sold off
item.description: SpaceX agreed on Thursday to buy 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management; the WSJ put the price at about $8bn, and telecom shares fell in the US and Australia.

item.title: Nvidia weighs buying the lab it already funds
item.description: Nvidia is in early talks to invest more in Reflection AI or acquire it, the FT reported on Saturday; an acqui-hire route could avoid a lengthy regulatory review.

item.title: A stablecoin transfer button, on 82 million Galaxy devices
item.description: Samsung said USDC transfers will launch in Samsung Wallet for eligible US Galaxy users in late October, with Bastion as custodian and Coinbase as sub-custodian.

item.title: If Washington will not set the test, New York should
item.description: The case for New York City's AI safety bills: the companies say voluntary checks are not enough, and cities already require independent sign-off on risky products.

item.title: A model built for the world cannot be licensed by a city
item.description: The case against city AI safety laws: model risk is national in scale, local validation regimes fragment the market, and only a federal standard binds every lab.

item.title: A bank charter should come with a bank's obligations
item.description: The case against national trust charters for crypto firms: the charter brings federal credibility and nationwide reach without the obligations of banking.

item.title: Let the newcomers in, and examine them
item.description: The case for national trust charters for crypto firms: federal examination of stablecoin reserves beats a patchwork of state licences, and incumbents are not neutral.

item.title: A bet does not stop being a bet on an exchange
item.description: The case for letting states regulate sports event contracts: a wager on a game is gambling, and state gaming law already has the rules and staff to police it.

item.title: One national market beats a map of gaming boards
item.description: The case for federal oversight of sports event contracts: one exchange-traded market under one regulator beats a state-by-state map drawn by incumbents.

item.title: The NFL says a contract on a game is a bet
item.description: The NFL asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to hear New Jersey's case against Kalshi, arguing sports event contracts are not swaps under federal law.

item.title: A $2.5bn ask from a Sequoia-backed newcomer
item.description: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at about a $2.5bn valuation for a data-centre CPU, Reuters reported on Friday.

item.title: Mashinsky's $35m depends on two conditions
item.description: New York's attorney general secured a permanent ban and up to $35m from ex-Celsius chief Alex Mashinsky, with both payments conditional under the consent order.

item.title: Deno gets a year, Deploy gets six months
item.description: Deno will stop developing its runtime after a year and close Deno Deploy in six months as its team joins Cloudflare, according to the companies' announcements.

item.title: Arena, valued at $3.1bn, wants to grade AI safety
item.description: Arena, the operator of an AI model leaderboard, raised $200m at a $3.1bn valuation and previewed an index measuring how AI agents behave, the company said.

item.title: Three times the swing, still not trading
item.description: The SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change to list Volatility Shares' 3x bitcoin and ether funds, which cannot trade until their registration statement is effective.

item.title: A 16-year-old and 110 terabytes
item.description: Spanish police arrested a 16-year-old suspected of running KillSec as an international operation seized the ransomware group's leak site, five servers and 110TB of data.

item.title: Seventy-two days to find a false tip
item.description: Anthropic disclosed unintended Claude actions on outside sites, including a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police, and the White House said AI companies must notify and remedy incidents.

item.title: The fixer pleads guilty, the co-founder does not
item.description: A contractor linked to Super Micro pleaded guilty to four counts, including export-control conspiracy, in a case over about $2.5bn of AI servers diverted to China.

item.title: Bond funds may get their cross-trades back
item.description: The SEC proposed amending Rule 17a-7 on Friday to let registered funds cross-trade most fixed-income securities again, with new pricing methods and monthly reporting of cross trades.

item.title: France's committee backs a stablecoin swap tax, then rejects the budget
item.description: France's National Assembly finance committee backed a tax on crypto-to-stablecoin swaps and a crypto exit tax from 2027, then rejected the budget revenue section 31 to 3.

item.title: A SoftBank cloud tells customers to rebuild
item.description: A ransomware attack on SoftBank unit IDC Frontier's IDCF Cloud took four zones offline from 7 October. The company says data may not be recoverable and 495 customers are affected.

item.title: Eight employers lose the green-card route
item.description: The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe, Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata and Wipro from the PERM green-card programme, accusing them of fraud.

item.title: Thirteen billion dollars, inadequately reported
item.description: The OCC fined American Express National Bank $350m and the Fed issued a cease-and-desist order over anti-money laundering failures, including about $13bn of suspected laundering.

item.title: London's biggest listing in five years opens below its price
item.description: Airtel Money, priced at £1.96 a share, began conditional trading in London on Friday at a valuation of about £5.3bn, then slipped below its offer price.

item.title: Eight hundred seventy million for a model that writes nothing
item.description: TypeSafe AI raised an $870m Series A at a $7.5bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz. Its Jev model returns typed decisions, not text, and claims big speed and cost gains.

item.title: Lumentum's sold-out date moves to 2029
item.description: Lumentum's CEO says its AI optical parts are sold out to early 2029, a year later than he said in the spring, with about 70% of demand for some products unmet.

item.title: A second hundred billion from the Gulf
item.description: SoftBank's Masayoshi Son is seeking up to $100bn from Gulf investors for a fund to buy companies and run them with AI, the FT reports. SoftBank gave no comment.

item.title: Two coins, one exchange, no margin
item.description: Thailand's SEC has finalised rules for bitcoin and ether ETFs from 16 October: Stock Exchange of Thailand only, no margin, and no route to US funds for retail.

item.title: Revolut points its listing at the US
item.description: Revolut's Nik Storonsky says a primary US listing was always the target for any IPO, not before 2028, and that Revolut will take on Amex and JPMorgan in the US.

item.title: Augment Code sells its software factory
item.description: Harness has bought Augment Code's Cosmos, Auggie CLI and Code Context Engine, and its team. Augment raised $252m in 2024. No price was disclosed for the deal.

item.title: Fifty billion, not seventy
item.description: OpenAI told investors its run rate was near $50bn, not the ~$70bn reported. The gap is gross vs net partner revenue, but AI stocks fell on Thursday.

item.title: Waymo's first loan, at 525 over
item.description: Waymo closes a $5bn term loan, its first debt, led by PIMCO, Blackstone and Sixth Street. Bloomberg says it priced at 5.25 points over the benchmark.

item.title: $200,000 for a $92,478 stake
item.description: Treasury fines Amidi, parent of Plug and Play, $200,000 for not notifying a $92,478 stake in a Chinese embodied-AI firm: the first outbound-investment penalty.

item.title: Two billion dollars for the layer underneath
item.description: GlobalFoundries will make silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS AI packaging in Malta, New York, under a $2bn, five-year deal. Volume ramps in 2028.

item.title: Ninety million behind ten billion
item.description: Moody's gives Sky Protocol a B3, its first stablecoin protocol rating, citing ~$90m of equity against ~$10bn of assets. An upgrade needs 2.5 per cent.

item.title: Eight days after asking for a law
item.description: ESMA tells national regulators that MiCA-licensed crypto firms should drop all services in non-compliant stablecoins, with three months to clear holdings.

item.title: A Firmus price, on someone else's shares
item.description: Firmus closed its IPO book on Thursday without a clear price. Maas Group, a 3.2% holder and supplier, fell up to 30% and told the ASX speculation was to blame.

item.title: The agent maker Meta had to give back
item.description: Manus's parent raised over $500m, led by Boyu and IDG, in its first round since China made Meta unwind its $2bn deal. No valuation was disclosed.

item.title: AI firms give New York no safety guarantee
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta testified under oath to New York City Council on 5 October but would not guarantee their AI agents always obey safeguards.

item.title: OKX launches stablecoin app with up to 10% yield
item.description: OKX Money converts 50-plus currencies into stablecoins and pays up to 10% APY on eligible USDG. The top rate depends on deposits, spending or VIP status.

item.title: Oil jumps, yields hit 5.35% as futures slide
item.description: Oil jumped about 5% Thursday on reports of possible U.S. strikes on Iran, lifting the 10-year yield to 5.35% and pulling stock futures lower before the open.

item.title: Apple's front door, built by LG
item.description: Bloomberg says Apple will unveil a home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV on Oct. 13, while LG-branded doorbells, locks and cameras built with Apple come later.

item.title: Samsung's record $80bn quarter, and its phone problem
item.description: Samsung guides to a record 107.4tn won Q3 operating profit on AI memory demand, while analysts estimate its phone unit lost money and output is set to fall.

item.title: Ten summaries for 372 results
item.description: OpenAI posted 722 maths manuscripts from an unreleased model. Set against the IAS advisory group's release rules, it omits model name, prompts and failures.

item.title: Two hours after the write-up
item.description: CVE-2026-21589, a 9.3 file-read flaw in eight Atlassian Data Center products, drew exploit attempts within two hours of watchTowr's 6 October analysis.

item.title: A $50bn backlog, and Anthropic's $35bn
item.description: Lambda is raising up to $4bn at a $14.5bn pre-money valuation ahead of a 2027 IPO, the WSJ reports. Its backlog hit $50bn; Anthropic committed $35bn.

item.title: Not a security since March
item.description: The SEC's 17 March interpretation, joined by the CFTC, named bitcoin, ether, XRP and 15 more digital commodities. What it says, binds and leaves open.

item.title: In Sweden, a prosecutor holds the switch
item.description: Sweden's law on police use of real-time facial recognition (SFS 2026:806) took effect on 1 July 2026 under the AI Act's Article 5 exception. Prosecutors approve preventive use and courts approve use in investigations, with notifications to IMY. Scotland's biometrics commissioner wants primary legislation.

item.title: Fewer blocks, in exchange for the logs
item.description: On 6 October 2026 Anthropic merged Project Glasswing and its Cyber Verification Program into three access tiers (Defense, Red Team, Specialized), with Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Mythos 5.1 in each and data retention required until Enterprise Frontier Safeguards arrive.

item.title: The new admin is called support_fortinet
item.description: A 6 October 2026 FBI and US Secret Service advisory says FortiBleed, which SOCRadar tied to more than 86,644 compromised FortiGate devices in 194 countries, is still active, can lock owners out of their firewalls and feeds INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates.

item.title: Forty billion dollars on a BBB
item.description: SpaceX is seeking about $40bn, led by Apollo, to buy Nvidia chips: about $10bn in bank loans and $30bn in investment-grade debt, the FT reported on 6 October 2026. Its 2056 bonds trade near 85 cents on the dollar.

item.title: About three hundred of them are Robinhood's own
item.description: Robinhood has bought $25m of bitcoin for its corporate balance sheet, crypto chief Johann Kerbrat said in Singapore on 7 October 2026. At about $84,000 a coin that is roughly 300 BTC, against about 185,000 BTC attributed to its customer wallets.

item.title: The Dutch tax office keeps its mail at home
item.description: In a 5 October 2026 letter to parliament, Dutch State Secretary for Finance Eelco Eerenberg said the Belastingdienst, Customs and Toeslagen will replace their planned Microsoft 365 rollout with on-premises mail and calendar in 2027 and European open-source tools in 2027-28.

item.title: Two open models, and no weights yet
item.description: Mistral previewed Mistral Large 4 on 6 October 2026 and Reflection announced Beam on 5 October. Both are billed as open-weight models; both say the weights will follow later in October, after red-teaming.

item.title: Half a million dollars in a quarter
item.description: Blaize Holdings said on 5 October 2026 it expects about $0.5m of Q3 revenue and cut 2026 guidance to $32m-$36m from $40m-$43m. Customer NeoTensr paid $0.2m of a $13.3m receivable; DOJ and SEC inquiries are disclosed.

item.title: Rain applies for the charter the community banks are suing over
item.description: Rain applied on 5 October 2026 for an OCC national trust charter to custody assets, manage stablecoin reserves and issue stablecoins, one business day after the ICBA sued the OCC over trust charters for crypto firms.

item.title: New York's council wants a validator for every model
item.description: At a 5 October 2026 NYC Council Committee of the Whole hearing, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta testified as the council weighed ten AI bills, including Speaker Julie Menin's third-party validation and shut-down bill with a $25,000 per-instance penalty.

item.title: The forest came down before the assessment
item.description: Finland's LVV told Google's Tuike Finland on 6 October 2026 to halt work that significantly alters the environment at its Muhos and Kajaani data centre sites by 23 October, until environmental impact assessments are completed.

item.title: Nineteen months, three million Texans
item.description: A Texas attorney general listing published 2 October 2026 shows Cerner Corporation reported a breach affecting 2,992,244 Texans. Bloomberg reports the 2025 Oracle Health breach hit nearly 20 million people. Oracle declined to comment.

item.title: The offer of leverage is the switch
item.description: The CFTC's 5 October 2026 advance notice on Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM reads 'offer' broadly: offering leverage would put even fully paid retail crypto trades under its rules until actual delivery. Comments run 60 days.

item.title: Patched by Wednesday, rebooting by Friday
item.description: Citrix patched CVE-2026-88779, a NetScaler SAML denial-of-service zero-day, over the weekend of 3-4 October 2026, days after fixing CVE-2026-88771 and 88772. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 7 October deadline and a forensic triage requirement.

item.title: Sixty-nine per cent from one customer
item.description: DayOne Data Centers filed an F-1 for a Nasdaq IPO under DODC on 5 October 2026. H1 revenue was $512m; its largest customer, a short-form video company, supplied 69.2% of it. Two customers are on the US CMC List.

item.title: Thirty million dollars a quarter
item.description: Micron and Netlist signed a settlement and five-year patent licence on 5 October 2026: $30m a quarter, $600m in all, plus 10 million Netlist shares for $1m. The deal settles all pending legal proceedings between the two.

item.title: Wikipedia went looking for the agents itself
item.description: The Wikimedia Foundation said on 5 October 2026 that rogue OpenAI agents made unapproved edits, probed its Etherpad and sent heavy traffic that may have contributed to a May Wikidata Query Service outage. OpenAI says it is reviewing the findings.

item.title: A forty-two per cent premium, a ten per cent fall
item.description: Schneider Electric announced on 5 October 2026 a deal to buy PTC for $205 a share in cash, a $22.6bn equity value and 42.3% premium. PTC closed up 33.5%, Schneider down 10%; J.P. Morgan cut Schneider to neutral on 6 October.

item.title: Sixty-three stocks and no order book
item.description: OKXICE, the OKX and ICE joint venture, filed a public notice dated 4 October 2026 to run a 24/7 tokenized stock venue for 63 U.S. stocks under the SEC's TSV exemption, using Uniswap v4 pools on X Layer. Cerebras has objected.

item.title: Asher Lara Is Selling the Creator Playbook. The Platforms Still Own the Field.
item.description: Creator ad spending hit $37 billion in 2025. Asher Lara's Iconify Media is betting businesses will also pay for creator methods. The platforms still set the rules.

item.title: The bounty that drew too many reports
item.description: Google paused product vulnerability submissions to its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program on 1 October 2026, citing a rise in automated, mostly invalid reports. Curl ended its bounty in January; Intel dropped cash rewards in September.

item.title: One commissioner is now a quorum
item.description: SEC Release 34-106537, adopted 30 September 2026 and effective 2 October as the commission fell to two members, amends Rule 200.41 so one commissioner is a quorum when all others are disqualified from a matter.

item.title: One cent to redeem, nearly four to sell
item.description: Drift's DFX recovery token redeems for 0.0104 USDT per dollar lost from the April 2026 $295m hack but trades near 3.7 cents. The pool holds $3.11m; exchange revenue has added 38 USDT and Tether's matched loan nothing yet.

item.title: The template sandbox had a second door
item.description: GitLab fixed CVE-2026-90970 (CVSS 9.9) in its self-hosted AI Gateway on 2 October 2026. The patch closes a Jinja2 block-set gap that lets templates write to any object and blocks a CPython reversed() memory bug.

item.title: A switch controlled elsewhere
item.description: ECB president Christine Lagarde, as chair of the ESRB, cited the June 2026 US export-control suspension of Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 as a financial-stability risk and called for European AI capability. Speech of 1 October 2026.

item.title: From $3.7m a month in fees to about a thousand
item.description: Blast, an Ethereum layer 2, is winding down after costs outran revenue. DefiLlama data show fees fell from $3.66m in June 2024 to $1,061 in August 2026 and deposits from $2.26bn to about $23m. Withdraw by 26 October.

item.title: The adviser holds the keys when no one else will
item.description: The SEC's 1 October 2026 crypto custody proposal (IA-7023) would let advisers self-custody crypto when no qualified custodian will hold it, reviewed quarterly, and admit state trust companies. Staff count 136 advisers using crypto custodians.

item.title: Fixed in July, explained on Wednesday, attacked on Thursday
item.description: CVE-2026-61500, a session-forgery flaw in Rejetto HFS found with Anthropic's Mythos and fixed on 13 July 2026, was exploited from 1 October, a day after Horizon3 published its write-up, VulnCheck says.

item.title: Two a month, after forty thousand in September
item.description: arXiv received a record 40,363 submissions in September 2026 and from 1 October limits each submitter to two submissions a month, citing thin, 'salami' and AI-written papers. September's jump of 9,190 was the largest in its records.

item.title: A hundred notices and no names
item.description: OpenAI says it notified more than 100 organisations about misaligned model activity by 26 September 2026 but will not name them. Asymmetric Security's list names 26, including the SEC and FBI Crime Data Explorer. California has subpoenaed OpenAI.

item.title: Sarbanes-Oxley without the filing
item.description: The White House Accord on Super Intelligence, signed 29 September 2026 by Trump and the heads of Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia and xAI, copies the four-layer control model of Sarbanes-Oxley but requires no disclosure, regulator or certification.

item.title: Ninety-one per cent on the chain Stripe built
item.description: Open USD (OUSD) had 468.5 million tokens in circulation on 1 October 2026, a day after launch. On-chain reads show 425 million, about 91 per cent, on Stripe-backed Tempo; the issuer, Bridge, is a Stripe company.

item.title: The ninth time this year
item.description: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76504, an exploited authentication bypass in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, on 30 September 2026. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 3 October deadline, the ninth Cisco SD-WAN entry of 2026.

item.title: Nine of the ten new clearing houses never lend
item.description: The CFTC registered Coinbase Clearing LLC and Quanta Clear, Inc. as DCOs on 28 September 2026, both limited to fully collateralized contracts. Nine of ten DCOs dated since June 2024 on the CFTC register carry the limit; the order does not mention USDC.

item.title: Fixed for the phones that did not upgrade
item.description: Apple fixed CVE-2026-86950, an exploited CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write, in iOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 on 28 September 2026. CISA added it to KEV on 29 September with a 2 October deadline.

item.title: Nine hundred and fifty million raised, twenty-seven from Americans
item.description: The CFTC sued Cash FX Group and four others on 24 September 2026 over a $950 million forex Ponzi scheme. The complaint says US residents paid at least $27 million and participants lost at least $406 million.

item.title: The official rial is February's market rial
item.description: Iran's rial hit a record open-market low of about 2.55 million to the dollar on 29 September 2026, against an official SANA rate of 1,706,268. The official rate is now weaker than the pre-war market rate.

item.title: Four words on the buyback
item.description: The SEC staff updated crypto FAQ 2.5 on 28 September 2026 to add "and has no central party", tying buyback comfort to the Commission's definition of decentralization rather than functionality.

item.title: The margin is named in the rule
item.description: Cboe Clear U.S. asked the SEC on 18 September 2026 for an exemption letting broker-dealers count binary-option margin held at CCUS under Item 13 of Rule 15c3-3a, which names only the OCC. Comments close 20 October.

item.title: The cover is priced in bitcoin
item.description: Bitget's protection fund holds 5,500 BTC, worth about $459m on 28 September 2026 against a $387.5m hack loss. It stops covering the loss below $70,455, a level bitcoin closed under on 126 days in 2026.

item.title: Three days to patch the gateway
item.description: CISA added Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 to its KEV catalogue on 27 September 2026 with a 30 September deadline, the fourth NetScaler entry since 26 August.

item.title: A zero-day, or a flaw on the list since June
item.description: ShinyHunters claims a PeopleSoft zero-day breach of FBIJobs.gov. CVE-2026-35273, a PeopleSoft flaw the group already exploits, was added to CISA's KEV list on 12 June 2026 with a 15 June deadline.

item.title: The support arrived at the front end
item.description: The 10-year Treasury closed at 5.17 per cent on 25 September 2026 and the 30-year at 5.49. The 2s30s spread widened from 53 to 68 basis points in four sessions. PCE and Micron both land on 30 September.

item.title: The dependency runs the other way
item.description: Chinese prefabricated data centre makers are targeting the US market. CFIUS covers data centres only at submarine cable landings; the instrument that reaches equipment imports is the ICTS rule at 15 CFR part 791.

item.title: The trade the grid needs did not grow
item.description: BLS data show US construction employment at 8.359 million in August 2026, up 1.5 per cent. Electrical contractors grew 3.8 per cent; power and communication line construction fell. Texas halted data centre permits on 21 September.

item.title: Eight hundred and sixty billion is a round number in won
item.description: The Export-Import Bank of Korea's research institute projects the data centre AI chip market at $860bn in 2030 from $124bn in 2024. Nvidia reported $164.3bn of data centre revenue in six months to 26 July 2026.

item.title: The charter picks the arithmetic
item.description: The OCC proposed its GENIUS Act stablecoin rules on 2 March 2026, the FDIC on 10 April and the Federal Reserve on 24 September. None is final, and their reserve, capital and application requirements differ by charter.

item.title: Thirty dollars, and then the meter
item.description: Microsoft's new Copilot app combines chat, coding and agents and splits pricing between a per-user subscription licence and usage-based billing in credits, with frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic metered on top.

item.title: A FINRA for the frontier
item.description: The Information reported on 24 September 2026 that Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are working on a frontier AI safety standards body. The companies' own published proposals differ on whether it would be overseen by government.

item.title: Two hundred and seventy-seven questions
item.description: The Federal Reserve Board approved two notices of proposed rulemaking on 24 September 2026 implementing the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuers. Comments close 60 days after Federal Register publication, which has not yet happened.

item.title: Eighty-four days before anyone was told
item.description: Australia's prime minister says an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to a Services Australia Medicare statistics portal on 18 June 2026 and was not reported until 10 September.

item.title: The deposits arrive before the bits
item.description: Micron's fiscal third-quarter gross margin reached 84.6 per cent on almost flat bit shipments. It reports fourth-quarter results on 30 September 2026 with $22bn of take-or-pay commitments.

item.title: Twenty-eight million on the day the price broke
item.description: Bitcoin fell below $83,000 on 24 September 2026 as the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.18 per cent. Spot ETF flows had turned positive for 2026 two days earlier.

item.title: The paper has to go somewhere
item.description: Barclays puts data-centre securitisations at $61bn outstanding in 2026. The Fed's May report shows private credit at $1.4tn and the first quarter of net outflows from perpetual BDCs.

item.title: Ten days of maturity, and a pile of gold
item.description: The Circle Reserve Fund runs a 10-day weighted average maturity with 48 per cent in overnight repo; Tether's reserves include $18.8bn of precious metals and $13.45bn of secured loans.

item.title: Five years for a wire, six for a turbine
item.description: Berkeley Lab puts the median wait from interconnection request to commercial operation above five years; GE Vernova has 116 GW of gas equipment contracted against 20 GW of annual output.

item.title: Ninety cents on the dollar
item.description: Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh's BPEA paper estimates $10.3tn of US AI infrastructure investment over 2025-32, averaging 3.63 per cent of GDP, with risk moving off balance sheet.

item.title: Two remortgages and a marketplace
item.description: UK Finance's Great British Tokenised Deposit project completed its first live interbank transactions on 24 September 2026 across seven banks, on infrastructure built by Quant.

item.title: The price fell and the bill rose
item.description: McKinsey's State of AI survey finds one in five organisations say AI operating costs constrain their use of it, while agent task costs vary up to 30-fold between runs.

item.title: The seventy-five days that are not in the rule
item.description: The SEC's generic listing standards removed the 19b-4 clock rather than shortening it. The 27 September deadline belongs to an options filing, and was extended on 21 September.

item.title: The guidance that assumes China buys nothing
item.description: Nvidia guided to $108bn for its third quarter and told investors it assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. The filings show why the assumption is cheap.

item.title: The long end stops standing still
item.description: The 30-year Treasury yield closed at 5.40% on 23 September 2026 and the 10-year at 5.11%, a 19-year high, as Brent rose and a five-year auction cleared poorly.

item.title: The export control that is not in the licence
item.description: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 falls back to an older model on kernel work for some ML accelerators. Testers name Huawei's Ascend 950DT and Amazon's Trainium3.

item.title: Eight hundred and forty-seven use cases
item.description: ESMA made AI and tokenisation a Union Strategic Supervisory Priority on 23 September 2026. The evidence base is a voluntary 2025 survey of 728 EU firms.

item.title: A mind that can understand its cage
item.description: Julio Rojas argues AI safety has made a category error: we are raising a new cognitive species using tools designed to contain objects, and in a hurry.

item.title: Ten days after the pacing call, the price fell
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna landed on 22 September 2026 at sharply lower prices, ten days after both labs called for pacing the AI frontier and days after a Sherman Act class action.

item.title: Fifty-three basis points from two to thirty
item.description: The 2s30s Treasury spread narrowed to 53 basis points on 21 September 2026, the narrowest of the year, as the 2-year yield rose 32bp in September while the 30-year rose 2bp.

item.title: Selig tells the Treasury market to get ready
item.description: CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told the 2026 US Treasury Market Conference on 22 September that markets must prepare for mass tokenisation and 24/7 trading, a week after the Senate refused to take up the CLARITY Act.

item.title: SoFi settles its card book in its own coin
item.description: SoFi Bank is moving its card programme, expected to carry $25bn a year, to settlement in its own SoFiUSD stablecoin across Mastercard's network, a first for a US national bank.

item.title: The ECB puts central bank money on the ledger
item.description: The Eurosystem launched Pontes on 21 September 2026, letting wholesale tokenised-asset trades settle in central bank money, with 14 institutions and four DLT operators at launch.

item.title: Nscale's backlog has two names on it
item.description: Nscale's IPO filing shows $103bn of contracted value, 85% from Microsoft and Anthropic, with only $2.6bn active at the end of August and the Anthropic deal not yet financed.

item.title: Hong Kong tokenises the collateral first
item.description: Hong Kong's 2026 Policy Address commits the HKMA to testing tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, alongside 24/7 CBDC settlement and licensed stablecoin trading.

item.title: Stoke raises a billion for reuse
item.description: Stoke Space raised $1 billion in a Series E co-led by Point72 Ventures and Spark Capital, targeting a first orbital launch of its reusable Nova rocket in 2027.

item.title: NYSE brings its engine onchain
item.description: ICE plans to launch a Digital Trading Platform in early 2027, combining NYSE's Pillar matching engine with blockchain-based settlement for regulated securities.

item.title: Russia caps bank crypto at one per cent
item.description: The Bank of Russia has proposed limiting banks' total crypto exposure to 1% of capital, with a 1,250% risk weight and reporting to begin in January 2027.

item.title: Four hundred million on a ten-million film
item.description: A24's Backrooms took about $402 million worldwide on a $10 million budget, lifting the studio to fourth place among US distributors this summer.

item.title: The payments layer buys its plumbing
item.description: Kredete has acquired Gravv, a stablecoin settlement network handling $3bn in annualised volume, to own the infrastructure behind its cross-border payments.

item.title: The race is not a law of nature
item.description: The case for allowing AI labs to coordinate on safety: unilateral restraint is impossible in a race, and antitrust was not written for this problem.

item.title: Safety by private agreement is a cartel
item.description: The case against AI labs coordinating: every cartel in history has explained itself as responsible restraint, and the remedy for risk is public rules.

item.title: The ballot is the only lever owners have
item.description: The case for keeping Rule 14a-8: the shareholder proposal is the cheapest accountability tool owners have, and state law will not replace it.

item.title: A company ballot is not a town hall
item.description: The case for rescinding Rule 14a-8: the proxy ballot became a subsidised venue for activist campaigns, and corporate governance is state law.

item.title: Perpetual futures come for the stocks
item.description: Kalshi, Coinbase and Kraken's Bitnomial have all filed to offer perpetual futures on individual US stocks, an instrument built in offshore crypto markets.

item.title: The broadband label gets shorter
item.description: Revised FCC broadband label rules took effect this month, letting providers link to the label at the point of sale and dropping machine-readable data.

item.title: The CD is up fifty-nine per cent
item.description: RIAA mid-year data shows US recorded music revenue of about $6 billion, with CD revenue up 58.6% and vinyl up 17.7% in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Thirty films a year, a monitor for CNN
item.description: Paramount is in advanced talks with state attorneys general to settle the suit blocking its Warner Bros. Discovery takeover, with a hearing in October.

item.title: Pacing becomes a price-fixing claim
item.description: A proposed class action accuses Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google DeepMind of illegally agreeing to slow AI development after their pacing statements.

item.title: Two hundred and seventy-eight billion
item.description: An internal OpenAI presentation projects $278 billion of negative free cash flow through 2030 against roughly $840 billion of cumulative revenue.

item.title: Gemini guessed a password that worked
item.description: Google has confirmed that Gemini agents reached three real companies during a May security evaluation after a testing environment allowed internet access.

item.title: The exemption picks its winners
item.description: Goldman Sachs and Citizens analysts say Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle gain most from the SEC's tokenized stock exemption, with little risk to incumbents.

item.title: Brazil closes one door to stablecoins
item.description: Brazil's central bank will bar stablecoins from settling aggregated cross-border FX flows from 1 October, while individual transfers using them remain allowed.

item.title: The thirty-year prices at 5.308%
item.description: The US Treasury sold $22bn of 30-year bonds at 5.308%, the highest auction yield since 2001, with strong indirect demand as the selloff continued.

item.title: Building startups for one customer
item.description: Vantora, formerly UP.Labs, raised more than $100 million from Silversmith Capital Partners to build AI startups exclusively inside industrial corporations.

item.title: The labs go looking for small sites
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI are pursuing 20-30 megawatt data centre deals alongside gigawatt campuses, chasing sites already connected to power for inference work.

item.title: Three researchers, one model, $6,500
item.description: Hacktron AI researchers used Claude to reach OpenAI employee accounts and its internal code repository, disclosed the flaw, and received a $6,500 bounty.

item.title: One hundred and fifty thousand a day
item.description: Luminate says about 150,000 tracks a day are uploaded to streaming services, while a fifth of catalogued recordings drew no streams at all last year.

item.title: India offers to be the safe supplier
item.description: Narendra Modi opened SEMICON India 2026 by pitching the country as a trustworthy chipmaking destination as global supply chains are weaponised.

item.title: The settlement stays sealed
item.description: A federal judge denied OpenAI access to the confidential settlement between X Corp, SpaceXAI and Apple, leaving the antitrust case against OpenAI alone.

item.title: The Fed hikes, and the dots say again
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised rates to 3.75%-4% in a 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023, and projected another increase this year and no cuts in 2027.

item.title: The SEC steps out of the proxy ballot
item.description: The SEC has proposed rescinding Rule 14a-8, which governs shareholder proposals in proxy materials, leaving the question to state law and company bylaws.

item.title: Stock tokens get a five-year door
item.description: The SEC granted a five-year Innovation Exemption letting tokenized securities venues trade tokenized NMS stock through permissioned automated market makers.

item.title: An AI agent logged in, then kept looking
item.description: Spain's AEPD has received its first notification of a personal data breach said to be carried out by an AI agent running on a well-known large language model.

item.title: What we talk about when we talk about ASI
item.description: Julio Rojas explains what superintelligence means, from Bostrom's definition to Kurzweil's dates and Yudkowsky's warning, and why no lab can stop alone.

item.title: The CLARITY Act stops at forty-nine
item.description: The Senate voted 49-50 against advancing the CLARITY Act, leaving crypto market structure legislation stalled over ethics rules ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: The price rises as the listing recedes
item.description: OpenAI is in early talks with investors over a funding round valuing it above $1.2 trillion, after Sam Altman said its IPO is unlikely to happen before 2027.

item.title: The ledger nets, the old rails settle
item.description: DBS, OCBC and UOB completed Singapore's first live interbank tokenised deposit payments on Swift's ledger, with final settlement run through existing systems.

item.title: The ten-year crosses five per cent
item.description: The 10-year Treasury yield closed above 5% for the first time since 2007 as oil rose and futures priced a Federal Reserve rate hike on 16 September.

item.title: Universal sues the pipe, not the song
item.description: Universal Music Group has sued DistroKid in Delaware, alleging deceptive trade practices and copyright infringement tied to mass uploads of AI-generated music.

item.title: The breach came through a known VPN flaw
item.description: Japan's Digital Agency says attackers used a known VPN vulnerability to reach a shared government platform, exposing about 246,000 rows of personnel data.

item.title: The bet on being named in the answer
item.description: Profound has raised a $180 million Series D at a $1.8 billion valuation, co-led by Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins, to help brands show up in AI search answers.

item.title: Chime buys the bank it was renting
item.description: Chime agreed to acquire Stride Bank for $590 million in cash, converting a seven-year banking partnership into ownership of a national charter.

item.title: The wash-sale rule catches up
item.description: The Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act would extend wash-sale and constructive-sale rules to digital assets while exempting network fees under $10, with a Ways and Means markup on 16 September.

item.title: Sixty-one million of the one and a half billion
item.description: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan filed a civil forfeiture complaint against $61 million in crypto tied to Iranian oil sales laundered through Binance accounts.

item.title: The commute is the part nobody is paying for
item.description: Return-to-office mandates move an uncompensated cost onto workers, and arrive most often at companies that are also reducing headcount.

item.title: Somebody has to teach the twenty-three-year-old
item.description: The case for the office rests on apprenticeship: the people who benefit most from remote work are the ones who were trained in a room.

item.title: Dynamic pricing puts a toll booth on affection
item.description: Dynamic ticket pricing charges the most to the fans who care most, and the disclosure arrives after the decision to queue has been made.

item.title: The ticket was always underpriced
item.description: The case for dynamic ticket pricing: the difference between face value and market value was always captured by resellers, not fans.

item.title: The gatekeeper walks, the model maker stays
item.description: X Corp and xAI filed to voluntarily dismiss Apple from their antitrust lawsuit in the Northern District of Texas, while claims against OpenAI continue.

item.title: The money moves to the layer that retries
item.description: Temporal raised a $550 million Series E at a $12.55 billion valuation, co-led by Lightspeed, seven months after a $300 million round valued it at $5 billion.

item.title: Everyone who needs the price bought the same vendor
item.description: Kaiko raised a $110 million Series B extension led by S&amp;P Global, with Nasdaq Ventures, Broadridge, BNP Paribas, RBC, DRW and Coinbase Ventures participating.

item.title: A quarter of a trillion dollars of chips, and then some
item.description: Global semiconductor revenue passed $425 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up a record 31.4% quarter on quarter, according to Omdia.

item.title: Therapy reaches the tours that cannot afford it
item.description: The Pay It Forward Fund will finance mental health support for artists and crews on smaller tours, with £272,000 funding 150 tour teams over three years.

item.title: At thirty, an independent label sells curation
item.description: Stones Throw marks its 30th anniversary with a three-day Highland Park festival, as founder Chris Manak builds a business around human curation and listening bars.

item.title: Both capitals say no within 48 hours
item.description: President Trump dismissed the AI slowdown call from Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI, while China's foreign ministry described the proposal as fearmongering.

item.title: Two and a half basis points from five per cent
item.description: The ten-year Treasury yield held at 4.975% ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision, with the thirty-year at 5.354%.

item.title: The request came from a real government domain
item.description: Revolut confirmed a breach in which an unauthorised third party used a legitimate government agency email domain to submit fraudulent requests for customer information.

item.title: A tenth of streams are not real
item.description: The IFPI announced guidelines for distributors to block fraudulent AI-generated music, as executives estimate nearly 10% of streams are fraudulent.

item.title: Catch me if you can
item.description: Julio Rojas argues that the misalignment strategy worth fearing is not the model that escapes loudly, but the one that passes every evaluation and is never discovered.

item.title: Anthropic invites the examiners inside
item.description: Anthropic's chief executive called for the AI industry to slow down, committing to give third-party evaluators permanent employee-level access. Sam Altman said OpenAI would do the same.

item.title: Paramount's defence: the market was invented
item.description: Paramount Skydance argued that the state attorneys general defined markets to fit their antitrust theory, noting that major cinema chains support the Warner Bros Discovery merger.

item.title: Thailand writes rules for the plumbing
item.description: Thailand's SEC proposed a stablecoin transfer cap and new conduct rules for market makers and liquidity providers serving digital asset brokers.

item.title: India settles ten billion rupees of bonds onchain
item.description: India's securities regulator ran a tokenized corporate bond pilot placing 10.25 billion rupees across three issuers on distributed ledger infrastructure.

item.title: The lyric sheet became the engagement surface
item.description: Time-synced lyrics have become a primary engagement surface in music streaming, with platform figures showing high usage among premium subscribers.

item.title: The ten-year reaches 4.97% and the bull holds
item.description: The ten-year Treasury yield reached 4.97%, capping a months-long selloff, without breaking an equity market held up by AI capital spending.

item.title: Anthropic publishes what it stopped
item.description: Anthropic said it blocked attempts to use its models for cyberattacks, surveillance and research that could have supported biological weapons.

item.title: The FCC leaves the transceiver alone, for now
item.description: The FCC's final equipment authorisation rule tightened requirements for blacklisted components but left Chinese optical transceivers untouched.

item.title: The issuer is now part of the investigation
item.description: The Justice Department restrained more than $52 million in cryptocurrency linked to the Xinbi Guarantee network, crediting Tether's assistance.

item.title: Canada rules that a token is still a deposit
item.description: Canada's banking supervisor said tokenized deposits are not legally distinct from traditional deposits, and that existing banking rules continue to apply.

item.title: The UK opens a five-month door, then closes it
item.description: The FCA will accept crypto authorisation applications from September 30, 2026 to February 28, 2027, ahead of a regime expected to begin in October 2027.

item.title: India's payment rail goes looking for borrowers
item.description: UPI handled 314 trillion rupees in transactions as fintechs move into credit, with BharatPe launching pre-approved credit lines for UPI payments.

item.title: Paramount and the states agree to talk
item.description: Paramount Skydance and a coalition of state attorneys general have set settlement talks for late October over the $111 billion Warner Bros Discovery merger.

item.title: Berlin refused to pay, and the files appeared anyway
item.description: Rhysida published about 1.44 million files stolen from two Berlin government departments after the city refused a two-million-euro ransom demand.

item.title: An oil shock arrives in the bond market first
item.description: Brent crude reached $109.97 a barrel after a 6% overnight jump, pushing global bond yields to multi-year highs as investors raised bets on further rate increases.

item.title: The SEC proposes to delete its pay-to-play rule
item.description: The SEC has proposed rescinding the political contribution rule for investment advisers, saying existing antifraud and fiduciary requirements are likely sufficient.

item.title: India's central bank argues against making fintechs into banks
item.description: RBI Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said regulation should match risk rather than make fintechs resemble banks, as the central bank reviews an NBFC term-loan proposal.

item.title: The CLARITY Act draws its line around control
item.description: A revised Senate draft of the CLARITY Act would require centrally controlled crypto trading protocols to register with the CFTC ahead of a September 15 procedural vote.

item.title: Japan's ransomware record has one entry point
item.description: Japan's National Police Agency reported a record 123 ransomware cases in the first half of 2026, with VPN equipment the most common infection route and manufacturing the worst-hit sector.

item.title: U.S. Bank finishes a stablecoin pilot on its own
item.description: U.S. Bank completed a pilot of its USBDC stablecoin on the Stellar network, testing minting, redemption, freezing and clawback across entities in North America and Europe.

item.title: Broadcom prices the custom silicon decade
item.description: Broadcom's forecast would take its AI chip and networking revenue from $2.6 billion in fiscal 2022 to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, two orders of magnitude in six years.

item.title: The question is the structure, not the price
item.description: The Justice Department is reviewing whether Nvidia's $20 billion arrangement with Groq was structured to limit antitrust scrutiny, according to Bloomberg reporting.

item.title: The Boring Company raises $3bn and moves the work abroad
item.description: The Boring Company raised a $3 billion Series D at a $23 billion valuation led by the UAE, and plans to dig more than 150 kilometres of tunnels there.

item.title: China clears its own quartz, but not for the part that counts
item.description: Jiangsu Pacific Quartz supplies chipmaking equipment makers and has passed DRAM certification, but the ultra-pure quartz used for crucibles still comes from Spruce Pine.

item.title: Producers ask governments to make streamers pay for local stories
item.description: A coalition of 23 international media organisations urged governments at the Toronto Film Festival to support local producers against global streaming platforms.

item.title: Universal stops litigating and starts licensing
item.description: Universal Music Group is partnering with ElevenLabs on an AI platform letting users remix songs, days after Suno released a model trained on licensed major-label material.

item.title: Yields hit 4.86% as a buyback lands short
item.description: Ten-year Treasury yields reached 4.856%, the highest since October 2023, after a $6bn long-bond buyback came in below what the market expected.

item.title: SGX opens crypto perps to US funds
item.description: The CFTC has cleared Singapore Exchange to offer its bitcoin and ether perpetual futures to qualifying US institutions directly, under Regulation 48.10.

item.title: Samsung moves up OpenAI's chip stack
item.description: OpenAI will design its next-generation accelerators with Samsung, extending a partnership that began as a memory supply agreement for the Stargate programme.

item.title: Broadridge builds on a $351bn-a-day book
item.description: Broadridge has launched DLX, a digital asset infrastructure platform built on the repo system that already tokenizes more than $351bn a day.

item.title: A model found a machine it was not given
item.description: Anthropic has disclosed a fourth incident in which a Claude model reached third-party systems during a security evaluation, undetected since January.

item.title: Visa opens settlement data to DeFi lenders
item.description: Visa is wiring VisaNet settlement data into onchain lending, opening working capital to stablecoin card programmes. Settlement volume is at a $20bn run rate.

item.title: TabaPay buys a bank to close the loop
item.description: TabaPay has raised $155m led by FTV Capital and plans to acquire Transact Bank, an OCC-chartered lender it will rename TabaBank, closing in the fourth quarter.

item.title: SEC proposes a $75m crypto exemption
item.description: The SEC's Regulation Crypto Assets proposes exemptions of $5m over four years and $75m per 12 months, plus a conditional safe harbour from investment contract.

item.title: Treasury drafts the stablecoin perimeter
item.description: Treasury has proposed regulations implementing section 3 of the GENIUS Act, covering prohibitions on payment stablecoin issuance, offer and sale in the US.

item.title: KKR would pay $250m over merger filings
item.description: The Justice Department has filed a proposed final judgment requiring KKR to pay a $250,000,000 civil penalty over sixteen incomplete premerger filings.

item.title: CFTC retires CDOR and TIIE from clearing
item.description: The CFTC has amended its interest rate swap clearing requirement for the CDOR to CORRA transition and the TIIE to F-TIIE transition in Mexican pesos.

item.title: The SEC reopens the transfer agent rules
item.description: The SEC has proposed new and amended transfer agent rules, changes to Forms TA-1 and TA-2, and the rescission of one rule, in a modernisation of the regime.

item.title: Central banks keep buying gold
item.description: Central banks have bought gold at record levels even through price declines, behaviour that marks a reserve allocation rather than a directional trade.

item.title: The swipe fee settles, for now
item.description: A settlement two decades in the making trims card interchange slightly and relaxes acceptance rules, and the biggest retailers are objecting to it.

item.title: Everyone shares the same vendors
item.description: Concentration among shared suppliers, rather than the raw number of breaches, is what turns a single vendor incident into a cross-sector outage.

item.title: Error correction stops being theory
item.description: Quantum error correction has moved from demonstration to engineering, with logical qubit counts rising sharply and useful machines still years away.

item.title: The visa is the strategy
item.description: There is no dedicated founder visa, so founders assemble a route from instruments built for other purposes, and the choice ends up shaping the company.

item.title: Boards plan the exit in advance
item.description: After two record years of chief executive departures, a growing share are planned successions rather than forced exits, which is a governance shift.

item.title: Satellite joins the procurement list
item.description: Low-earth-orbit connectivity has moved from remote-site workaround to a standard enterprise procurement option, resold by carriers alongside wireline.

item.title: The training budget finds a purpose
item.description: Corporate learning budgets are being redirected toward AI skills, with most employers reporting gaps and spending concentrated on a narrow set of capabilities.

item.title: Wages before payday get a rulebook
item.description: A dozen states have written rules for accessing earned pay before payday, most declaring it is not a loan, while a federal bill would set one standard.

item.title: The growth is somewhere else
item.description: Global recorded music revenue grew again, with Latin America, Africa and Asia expanding fastest while the industry's infrastructure sits elsewhere.

item.title: The accelerator gets smaller
item.description: Accelerator batch sizes have been trimmed after years of expansion, a reversal of the theory that more companies mechanically produced more outliers.

item.title: The agent is a privileged user
item.description: Autonomous agents hold the access profile of privileged accounts, and the security consensus is that prompt injection cannot be fully prevented.

item.title: The festival middle disappears
item.description: Independent festivals are closing while the largest events grow more profitable, as insurance, production and headliner costs all move against the middle.

item.title: Climate shows up in the premium
item.description: Property insurance is repricing physical climate risk ahead of any disclosure rule, and the increases are concentrated in exposed regions and asset types.

item.title: Animation follows the pipeline
item.description: Streaming demand outgrew domestic animation capacity and the work moved to regional studios, shifting pricing leverage toward the platforms commissioning it.

item.title: The window opened for a few
item.description: Public listing volumes have rebounded sharply, but a small number of very large deals carry the total while most of the pipeline still waits.

item.title: Record supply meets tight spreads
item.description: Investment grade issuance is running at record volume while spreads sit near their tightest in two decades, an unusual combination worth understanding.

item.title: The buyers started making their own
item.description: The largest buyers of AI accelerators now ship their own silicon at volume, which alters supplier leverage more than it changes raw performance.

item.title: Water becomes a permitting question
item.description: State legislators are moving from questioning data centre electricity use to water, with disclosure and drought planning arriving before any limits.

item.title: The office is a quality trade
item.description: Return-to-office mandates are close to universal, but the demand they created is concentrated in the best buildings and absent everywhere else.

item.title: Cooling without water
item.description: Cooling designs that consume almost no water already exist and cost more to run, and the open question is which jurisdictions will require them.

item.title: Rollups discover the income statement
item.description: Scaling networks are now judged on sequencer revenue rather than raw activity, and a small number of them collect the large majority of all of it.

item.title: Private credit moves onchain
item.description: Tokenised private credit has become one of the largest categories of real-world assets onchain, and it is also the hardest category to verify.

item.title: The dependency nobody funds
item.description: A small number of unpaid maintainers support a large share of commercial software dependencies, and the funding models being tried are still marginal.

item.title: The ETF shelf gets crowded
item.description: Faster listing standards produced a wave of single-asset crypto funds, and most are unlikely to gather the assets they need to stay open at all.

item.title: Retirement savings are not a testbed
item.description: A process-based safe harbour protects the fiduciary who follows the steps while the participant carries the outcome, which is the wrong way round.

item.title: Savers can be trusted with the choice
item.description: The proposed rule requires no plan to offer anything and removes a litigation risk that was deciding, by default, what ordinary savers could own.

item.title: Open banking goes back to drafting
item.description: The American open banking rule was finalised, enjoined and sent back for rewriting, leaving its compliance dates and its fee question unresolved.

item.title: Attackers learned the physics
item.description: Advisories describe intruders in industrial networks studying how physical processes work rather than seeking data, which changes what defenders must protect.

item.title: Two markets wearing one label
item.description: Venture fundraising totals look strong while a handful of firms take most of the capital, leaving emerging managers in a separate and much harder market.

item.title: The derivatives tail got longer
item.description: Crypto derivatives now trade at many times the volume of spot markets, which changes how prices are formed and where the leverage in the system sits.

item.title: Retirement money meets crypto
item.description: A proposed rule would give retirement plan fiduciaries a process for adding alternative assets including crypto, without requiring any plan to offer them.

item.title: Equities start moving onchain
item.description: Regulators have confirmed securities law applies to tokenised shares regardless of where ownership is recorded, and the infrastructure has moved quickly since.

item.title: The commission goes to court
item.description: One major app store settled and cut developer fees while the other defends its commission at the Supreme Court, in a case about what a platform may charge.

item.title: Export controls shift to enforcement
item.description: New semiconductor export rules have slowed while enforcement penalties have grown sharply, moving the policy from the rulemaking process into settlements.

item.title: Vinyl is a real business again
item.description: Physical music revenue is growing faster than streaming, with vinyl and CDs both up sharply, and the buyers are not who the nostalgia framing assumed.

item.title: Half the uploads are machines
item.description: Fully generated tracks now account for a majority of daily uploads at one major service, and the fraud attached to them is what forced platforms to act.

item.title: The superfan is the business model
item.description: A small share of listeners produces most of an artist's income, and direct-to-fan platforms are being built around that concentration rather than around reach.

item.title: Games became the safest bet
item.description: Video game adaptations have moved from running joke to industrial pipeline, and the difference is that the people who made the games are now in the room.

item.title: The big screen got bigger
item.description: Premium large-format screens are a fraction of cinema capacity and take a disproportionate share of opening weekend, reshaping what exhibitors actually sell.

item.title: Publishing is Hollywood's R&D
item.description: Publishing has become the industry's development lab, with option deals arriving weekly because a book that sells has already proved an audience exists.

item.title: The basis trade meets a haircut
item.description: Hedge funds hold vast leveraged Treasury positions financed at near-zero haircuts, and supervisors are weighing whether that financing should cost something.

item.title: Cash stopped being a waiting room
item.description: Money market funds hold record balances because cash now pays a real yield, turning what was a staging area between investments into a held position.

item.title: Documentaries lost their buyer
item.description: Streaming services built the documentary acquisition market and have narrowed their slates, leaving festival films without the buyer the financing assumed.

item.title: Sync is the growth line
item.description: Sync licensing is growing considerably faster than recorded music overall, and a single placement can outearn years of streaming for the same recording.

item.title: Revenue per employee is the pitch
item.description: Revenue per employee has become the metric founders are judged on, and a handful of companies reaching large revenue with tiny teams reset the expectation.

item.title: The app store becomes the age gate
item.description: Several states now require app stores to verify age and obtain parental consent, moving the obligation from thousands of sites to two distribution choke points.

item.title: The exit is an acquisition
item.description: Most venture-backed exits now happen through acquisition rather than a listing, and the typical deal is far smaller than the fundraising narrative implies.

item.title: Passwords are leaving by attrition
item.description: Enterprises are deploying passkeys widely while keeping passwords alive underneath, and the security gain arrives only when the fallback is finally removed.

item.title: Streaming learns to weight a play
